body:
Independent fresh-context reviews of this change, in a fresh read-only context that did not author it. Six rounds, each on the exact head of the round.

| round | head | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `6705cf5` | REQUEST CHANGES |
| 2 | `b0d8cf0` | APPROVE |
| 3 | `5c4db44` | APPROVE WITH NITS |
| 4 | `4c53c6a` | REQUEST CHANGES |
| 5 | `6659ac3` | REQUEST CHANGES |
| 6 | `587fe8e` | not run |

Every finding of every round was fixed, and each fix has a regression test that fails without it. What the rounds found:

- The digits of another script -- the fullwidth digits, the Arabic-Indic digits -- were counted by no alternative and were dropped: a date written with the fullwidth digits counted three of its nine characters. The group of digits is now every digit Python knows.
- The class of the characters of those writings was short three times over: it stopped before the Kangxi radicals, then before the jamo and the extensions G and H of the ideographs, then before the halfwidth hangul, the Hangzhou numerals and the vertical marks of the Japanese writing, and last before the kanbun, the enclosed letters and months and the circled ideographs. It now holds the twenty-five blocks of those writings whole, and a test holds one character of every block, so that no block can be dropped.
- The justification of the rule was false: the count does not claim what a tokeniser of a model provider does, which is not true of every one of those characters. The count is an estimate and the wording says so.
- The digits are counted in groups of up to three, which is what the rule does.

What the reviews verified, each on the exact head of its round: every character of every script is counted by some alternative or is whitespace; the count of ordinary Latin text is unchanged; the count of a text that arrives in pieces does not depend on where it was split; the buffer of the carried text stays bounded; and the figure quoted in the README and the changelog was reproduced exactly, all twenty-one numbers of it, against the `cl100k_base` tokeniser built offline from the vocabulary of the `tiktoken-offline` wheel.

The review of the last head has not been run. The `CI` and `dco` checks are green on it.
